title: StrataLogix inference model path and deployment scouting
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
summary: Intro call to understand StrataLogix requirements for long-context, multilingual document understanding and step-by-step tool-calling (data lookup + geocoding). Customer leaning toward private/Dedicated for compliance but wants cost/latency trade-offs and open model benchmarking. Agreed to run a small eval: 1 week bench with 8k and 32k context tests and a tool-calling prototype on Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated baseline.
next_steps: Redwood to share model perf matrix and pricing sheet (Jenna)
SE to provision benchmark harness and sample prompts (Samir)
Customer to provide 3 sample long-doc prompt sets and schema for tool calls (Priya)
Schedule a 1-hour follow-up demo with tool-calling prototype next Tuesday
action_items: Samir Patel - create benchmark harness for 8k and 32k context (due 2028-11-02)
Jenna Morales - send pricing and hosted vs dedicated vs private comparison doc (due 2028-10-31)
Priya Singh - upload 3 anonymized prompt sets + tool schema to shared drive (due 2028-11-01)
Ethan Cole - share compliance checklist and data residency constraints (due 2028-11-03)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-10-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jenna (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Riley (Redwood SE), Marina (CTO - StrataLogix), Diego (ML Eng), Priya (PM), Ethan (SRE)

[00:00] Jenna Morales: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jenna from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We also have Samir and Riley from our solutions engineering team. Could you do a quick intro on your side?
[00:07] Marina Voss: Yeah hi, I'm Marina, CTO at StrataLogix, we do large-scale geospatial doc ingestion, lots of multi-page reports and imagery meta. Diego and Priya will be the day-to-day.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: hey, Diego here, ML infra and model selection.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Priya product, focusing on workflows, esp tool-calling for live lookups.
[00:18] Jenna Morales: great, thanks. High level, we want to learn about your workloads, constraints, and success criteria. Samir, do you want to jump in?
[00:25] Samir Patel: Sure. First question: how long are the typical documents you need to include in context? You mentioned long docs in the signup.
[00:31] Priya Singh: It's variable, but many of our reports are 10-15k tokens after OCR, some combined threads push toward 30k when we include images' extracted text and appendices. For retrieval-augmented flows we need 8k coverage as baseline and occasional 32k-ish sessions for full report re-reads.
[00:45] Riley Cho: okay that explains it, so both 8k steady and 32k peak. Are you expecting token-level pricing to be a primary constraint?
[00:53] Marina Voss: cost matters but reliability and compliance are the blockers. We process sensitive client geodata so audit logs, KMS, and VPC/on-prem options are important. SOC 2 is a must, and we have to support EU data residency for some clients.
[01:05] Samir Patel: understood. On Redwood side we offer Hosted, Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem). For regulated data Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane and KMS integrations, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation without managing infra. Hosted is fastest to iterate. For long context we support models and KV cache strategies to keep repeated prefixes cached to reduce cost.
[01:25] Diego Alvarez: question, how mature is the KV cache across token sizes? any gotchas with 32k?
[01:29] Samir Patel: it's fairly mature but depends on the model variant and kernel path. We do prefix cache and continuous batching; for 32k you might need higher memory instances and adjusted batching windows. There's also quantization tradeoffs - 4-bit models save cost but sometimes degrade exactness on code/structured outputs.
[01:45] Priya Singh: on the models themselves, we're leaning open-source. We tried Llama 3 and Mistral in POCs earlier. Can you run comparisons?
[01:53] Samir Patel: absolutely. We usually benchmark Llama 3 family, Mistral-Instruct, and emerging 32k-capable open variants. We can run both generation quality and latency/cost profiles. For multilingual support we look at instruction-tuned models vs multilingual-specific like XLM-based models, but many of the recent Llama and Mistral forks are surprisingly good on EU languages.
[02:13] Marina Voss: also need reliable tool-calling. Our workflows: user asks a question, model issues a geocode lookup (external API), then a filter step against a policy engine, then returns structured JSON. We need function calling that is deterministic and auditable.
[02:26] Riley Cho: Redwood supports structured function/tool calling and trace logs. We capture token-level latencies and can persist call results in audit logs; if you need stronger immutability we can forward to your SIEM.
[02:36] Ethan Cole: for SSO and RBAC, we use Okta. How deep is SAML/SCIM support for private deployments?
[02:42] Samir Patel: full SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning in Private and Dedicated. Hosted has standard SSO but you can opt into enterprise SAML. For keys we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM for Private.
[02:55] Priya Singh: latency targets — we need sub-200ms for short tool calls, but document-level reasoning can be slower. How do you handle routing?
[03:02] Riley Cho: we have smart routing policies — route by latency buckets and cost. For small calls you hit low-latency runtime; for 32k sessions we route to high-memory hosts. We can also set automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants if latency budgets allow.
[03:16] Diego Alvarez: what's the typical throughput for Dedicated? we need baseline for 100 qps synthetic queries across 8k sessions.
[03:22] Samir Patel: depends on GPU size; with dedicated pool you tune concurrency and autoscale spikes. We can share a performance matrix, but ballpark an A100-class Dedicated pod can handle many concurrent 8k sessions if you batch aggressively. We'll validate with a benchmark.
[03:35] Marina Voss: about data residency — can Dedicated be provisioned in EU region only?
[03:39] Jenna Morales: yes, Dedicated capacity can be pinned to regions, and Private gives you full control for an on-prem option.
[03:45] Priya Singh: tooling: we plan to call three external endpoints in prototype: geocode, license-check (policy), and a vector DB lookup. How do we wire that in securely?
[03:54] Riley Cho: tool-calling supports signed request patterns and we can host a proxy in your VPC to handle secrets. We also log the inputs and outputs for audit and can redact tokens.
[04:05] Samir Patel: also worth noting how we test: for tool calls we record the sequence and can replay for debugging; you can enforce deterministic outputs by pinning model seeds and using temperature 0 for lookups.
[04:16] Diego Alvarez: interesting — any limits on number of functions? we might have a dozen microservices to call.
[04:20] Riley Cho: no hard cap, but performance depends on orchestration latency; for complex workflows we recommend bundling calls or using an orchestration layer.
[04:28] Priya Singh: let's talk models — if we want a 32k-capable open model with decent multilingual behavior and reliable JSON structured outputs for tool-calling, what do you recommend?
[04:36] Samir Patel: currently we'd recommend a staged approach: benchmark a 8k Llama 3 variant (fast, cheaper), a Mistral-Instruct 32k variant if available, and a quantized 32k variant for Dedicated to check cost. If accuracy on multilingual legal Portuguese/Spanish is key, add a multilingual-tuned checkpoint. We'll include Rouge/BLEU-style task evals and prompt-sensitivity checks.
[04:58] Marina Voss: are there known hallucination deltas across quantized vs fp16? we can't have bad policy outputs.
[05:04] Samir Patel: yes hallucination risk rises with aggressive quantization, and structured JSON can break if tokenization changes. We recommend rule-based post-processors and a small verification model in fp16 for final checks in critical flows.
[05:20] Priya Singh: curious about price delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our approximate load — can you ballpark?
[05:26] Jenna Morales: we'll send a pricing sheet; Hosted is per-token, good for pilot. Dedicated is committed monthly and becomes cost-effective at sustained load; Private has platform fees plus infra. We'll include an example calc for your expected 100 qps 8k baseline and peak 32k bursts.
[05:45] Diego Alvarez: sample prompts: we'll give you three long-doc workflows and a few short tool-call sequences. Expect mixed languages - EN/ES/PT.
[05:52] Samir Patel: perfect. For benchmarking we'll run generation accuracy, tool-calling correctness, latency p95, and cost per 1k tokens. Also we'll run multilingual tests on the same prompts.
[06:03] Riley Cho: timeline? we can stand up a hosted prototype within 48hrs and spin a Dedicated benchmark in ~5 business days.
[06:10] Marina Voss: we'd like both — quick hosted prototype to validate function-calling and then Dedicated bench for perf/cost. If Dedicated looks good we'll talk Private for EU compliance.
[06:20] Jenna Morales: sounds like a plan. Any other constraints we didn't ask about?
[06:23] Ethan Cole: retention rules — we cannot have raw text retained outside EU region for certain customers; can we set token retention policies?
[06:29] Samir Patel: yes, retention is configurable per-tenant in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports retention policies but for strict residency Private is preferred. We'll document retention controls.
[06:40] Priya Singh: one more on monitoring — can Redwood expose per-route token-level cost and traces to our Datadog?
[06:46] Riley Cho: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward metrics to Datadog/Prometheus; token-level cost breakdowns available in Console.
[06:52] Marina Voss: any compliance pack we can review?
[06:55] Jenna Morales: I'll include SOC2 Type II report, ISO docs, and our security whitepaper in the follow-up email.
[07:02] Diego Alvarez: cool. Let's capture next steps and deadlines.
[07:05] Jenna Morales: quick recap: Redwood to deliver model perf matrix, pricing, SOC2 docs; SE to provision bench and prototype; StrataLogix to share prompts and compliance checklist; schedule a follow-up demo next Tuesday. Anything to add?
[07:16] Priya Singh: looks good. Add a small note: we'd like a canary strategy for Dedicated before migrating production.
[07:20] Samir Patel: noted — we'll propose canary rollout steps.
[07:23] Marina Voss: thanks everyone, excited to see the prototype.
[07:26] Jenna Morales: thanks all, we'll follow up, bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps, some model names may be mis-transcribed (Llama/Lama), mention of KV cache as "K V cache" in audio. References: shared drive link placeholder: https://redwood.app/drive/stratalogix-prototype (demo materials will be posted there).
